payload.explanation: After releasing and retreating in step place_u_brown, u_brown's measured pose (x=0.40595, y=-0.14154, z=0.05719, quat=[-0.68116,0.19635,0.13495,0.69228)) deviates from u_brown_placement (x=0.40278, y=-0.15087, z=0.04538, quat=[-0.70711,0,0,0.70711]) by 0.0477m position and ~27.5deg orientation, both outside the object's registry tolerances (0.01m, 10deg). Believed mechanism: the part likely caught on the slot edge or slipped slightly off-square during the final descent and did not fully seat into the fixture before release. Attempting a reseat before closing this step.

payload.explanation: All four parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) reached their final placement frames within registry tolerance by run end; u_brown and line_green each required one reseat after an initial out-of-tolerance placement (both corrected, see valid_variation verdicts on those steps), and u_orange and inverted_u_yellow seated correctly on the first attempt. However, during the first (failed) u_brown insertion attempt, the off-square descent contacted base1 and nudged it by ~1.3cm position / ~3.3deg yaw (detected by watch_base1, recorded as observation obs-002). This is a standing violation of the invariant that base1, the fixture, is never picked and must remain undisturbed: the fixture's physical position was permanently altered and was not, and could not be, restored to its original pose -- all four seatings are correct only relative to the fixture's new, disturbed location. Per the run-verdict rules, a standing uncorrected violation makes the run non_conformant regardless of the parts' own correct end states. No bystander (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) moved at any point -- all four bystander disturbance monitors and the base2 watch stayed un-fired for the whole run. An unidentified small object with no registry TF frame was observed on the bench throughout (obs-001); it is outside the task's object set and its movement/non-movement carries no conformance weight here.
